newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran sees little hope for Cairo conference.
newsitem.headline: Iran sees little hope for Cairo conference.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Tuesday said the Middle East economic conference in Cairo had little hope of success because of increasing Arab-Israeli differences.

"Differences between the Zionist regime (Israel) and Arab countries have sharpened because of Tel Aviv's failure to carry out earlier agreements...Given these disputes, observers do not have much hope regarding the outcome of the Cairo economic conference," state-run Tehran radio said.

In a commentary on the third annual Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference, the radio said it was being held to "give the impression that the process of compromise (peace) was advancing and to create hope for its future".
Iran says Israel has no right to exist. Tehran has opposed the peace process as a sell-out of Palestinian and Arab rights.
Businessmen and officials fron 92 countries are taking part in the conference which was originally aimed to integrate Israel into the region's economy.
Tehran radio said the conference was also threatened by conflicts between Europe and the United States. The European Union has sought a more active role in the U.S.-driven Middle East peace process.

Iranian newspapers on Tuesday blasted the conference, with the daily Jomhuri Eslami saying it was designed "not only for peace with an occupying enemy, but for the unconditional surrender of the Arabs".
